newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: J.Martins wants to buy up to 1.5 pct BCP.
newsitem.headline: J.Martins wants to buy up to 1.5 pct BCP.

text.p: Portugal's second biggest retailer Jeronimo Martins (JM) would like to buy gradually up to 1.5 percent of Banco Comercial Portugues (BCP), Portugal's biggest private bank, JM Finance Director Jorge Ponce de Leao said.

"It will be an acquisition of shares over time. The objective is 1.5 percent," Ponce de Leao told Reuters. "(The acquisition) could take place over a long period. The idea is not to create tensions in the market."

JM and BCP said on Wednesday that they had signed an agreement to launch a private bank owned equally by both groups that would offer in-store financial services to customers in JM hypermarkets and supermarkets.
Ponce de Leao did not rule out eventually buying more than 1.5 percent of BCP's capital.
"I won't say no," he said. "But banking is not our core business."

BCP, listed on the Lisbon, New York and Frankfurt stock exchanges, has total assets of 5.3 trillion escudos ($34.8 billion), total deposits of 4.1 trillion escudos and total loans of 2.1 trillion escudos.
It has a market capitalisation of about 246 billion escudos.

JM's total turnover was more than 256 billion escudos in 1995. The group, listed on the Lisbon stock exchange, has more than 130 outlets, including supermarkets, hypermarkets and "cash and carry" shops. It has a market capitalisation of about 184 billion escudos.
